text:
Carla: quick sync — ran a focused streaming vs non-streaming apples->oranges test to isolate client pacing + KV warmup bias. posting raw notes.
Mike: nice, what's the harness? replay or synthetic?
Carla: replay harness with controlled inter-chunk delays. also ran synth with identical per-request spacing to compare.
Aj: sweet. did you disable autoscaling and routing fallbacks? those can hide regressions.
Carla: yes — single pinned kernel, no fallback, fixed batch size 8. KV cache state toggles: cold, partially-warm (50%), fully-warm.
Sasha: can you paste the runner command?
Carla: sure:
```
./replay-runner --trace-id=run-2026-03-18 
  --mode=streaming 
  --client-pacing-ms=50 
  --batch-size=8 
  --kernel=amp-attn-v2 
  --kv-warmup=half 
```
Mike: baseline (nonstream) latency p50/p95?
Carla: nonstream, cold KV: p50=42ms p95=128ms. streaming, cold KV: p50=36ms p95=210ms (tail blown out).
Aj: interesting — tail is worse with streaming when KV cold. suggests backpressure + readloop retries or chunk requeueing.
Sasha: any CPU stalls or scheduling spikes in the profiler?
Carla: yes — perf trace shows readloop worker hitting repeated sleeps and queue churn. snippet from perf-bot:
```
perf-bot: readloop_core: avg wakeups 12/s, avg queue_time 18ms, kernel_switches spike aligned w/ KV fetches
```
Aj: that matches hypothesis: streaming readloop issues amplify KV miss penalties because partial responses keep client sockets open longer and continuous batching can't absorb latency.
Mike: did you try increasing client pacing to 100ms to let KV catchup?
Carla: did that. p95 improved for streaming (down to ~140ms) but throughput dropped ~18%. nonstream unaffected.
Sasha: so there's a tradeoff: keep low pacing for throughput but tail suffers on cold KV. We should document a recommended warmup strategy and perhaps a server-side soft-throttle to avoid pathological tails.
Aj: another idea: temporarily switch kernel selection on cold KV to a lower-latency KV path (even if slightly more expensive) until cache warmed. kernel-hint on request.
Mike: agree. we can add routing policy rule: if kv_hit_rate < 0.6 then force kernel=kv-fast-fallback. cheap to implement?
Carla: prototype results look promising: when forcing kv-fast-fallback at 40% miss rate, streaming p95 drops from 210ms -> 115ms, throughput stable. cost regression ~6%.
perf-bot: note: regression tests flagged two existing perf tests that assumed streaming tail was always better — need to update expectations.
Sasha: can you attach the raw numbers and config diff to the PR? I'll write a short ops runbook recommending: warmup windows, client pacing defaults, and kernel-hint policy.
Carla: will do. also flagging follow-ups:
- measure multi-tenant effects (we ran single-tenant)
- test with autoscaling on (how does fallback interact)
- add a microbenchmark for readloop queue backpressure
Mike: thanks — also please include exact replay trace used (so others can apple->orange).
Carla: uploading trace to s3://redwood-perf/1918765432/replay.tr.gz and opening PR with results. cc @Aj @Sasha :thumbsup:
ops-bot: created ticket PERF-1178 "client pacing + KV warmup policy" assigned to eng-runtime
Mike: awesome. small next step: can someone schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to decide whether kernel-hint shipped behind feature flag?
Aj: I can lead that. 10am PT works for me.
Carla: adding calendar invite.
